key_findings.finding: A thin-strut (71-µm) CoCr stent with nano-thin Polyzene-F coating versus bare-metal control in pigs had significantly less neointimal thickness at 28 and 90 days (p=0.023, 0.005), numerically reduced inflammation (p=0.06, 0.13), and similar endothelial coverage; coating also reduced monocyte adhesion and thrombus formation in ancillary assays. This suggests benefit for neointima without impaired endothelial coverage, but inflammation comparisons were not conventionally significant.

Polymer-free nanoporous paclitaxel stents versus polymer-based sirolimus stent and BMS in minipigs showed more complete endothelialization at day 14 than SES (BMS reached 100% coverage); high-dose nano-PES reduced neointimal hyperplasia versus BMS at day 28, but low-dose did not. Nano-PES had less fibrin and inflammation than SES; this is a mixed but potentially favorable response dependent on drug dose.

source_tools.relevance: direct porcine comparison of polymer-free design and vascular healing

key_findings.finding: In a porcine randomized study of BMS, polymer-free probucol, sirolimus, and dual-drug polymer-free stents, probucol stent strut coverage at 14 days was 53.2% versus 20.3% for SES (p=0.002), but dual-drug polymer-free stents did not improve endothelialization overall; no animal had angiographic thrombosis or MI. Abstract-level reporting does not establish consistent restenosis/neointimal advantages.

source_tools.relevance: comparative porcine study endothelialization and thrombosis

key_findings.finding: Evidence across direct animal comparisons suggests stent design can favorably alter vascular response, especially thinner/improved platforms or selected polymer-free/coated designs, but effects are not uniform: thick-strut bioabsorbable EES and biolimus stents showed greater acute thrombogenicity than thin-strut biodegradable-polymer EES, and only BMS achieved complete re-endothelialization by day 28 in the separate healing comparison. Overall conclusion is qualified, not a universal design benefit; studies differ in model (some endpoints from rabbit or ex-vivo assays) and designs bundle multiple features.
